Authors: Choudhary, Prashant Kumar; Innan, Nouhaila; Shafique, Muhammad; Singh, Rajeev
Source_Title: Quantum Machine Intelligence
Evidence_Location: Full_Text; Abstract p.1; §3.1 p.6; §3.2–3.3 pp.6–10; Table 2 p.11; §4.2–4.7 pp.11–15; Data Availability p.17; dataset citation p.18
Coding_Notes:
Full-text verified against HQNN-FSP (Quantum Machine Intelligence, 2026;
DOI: 10.1007/s42484-026-00390-9). The study evaluates a custom QNN
regressor and two hybrid quantum-classical architectures (HybridQNN1
and HybridQNN2) for continuous stock-price prediction. Inputs include
historical OHLC data and technical indicators such as RSI, MACD, ADX,
SMA50 and SMA200 from a Nifty-100 5-minute stock dataset. The target
is closing-price regression, and the study explicitly discusses
next-day forecasting.

The data are split in a time-ordered manner and TimeSeriesSplit is used;
however, conventional random k-fold cross-validation is also evaluated.
The authors explicitly acknowledge that random k-fold allocation may
introduce information leakage by allowing future observations to enter
training folds. Therefore, Validation_Design=Random_Shuffled,
Chronological_Split=Yes, Leakage_Risk=High, and the passage-verified
leakage mechanism is Random or shuffled splitting.

SelectKBest feature selection and MinMax scaling are reported, but the
paper does not clearly establish that these preprocessing operations
were fitted exclusively on the training data; therefore,
Preprocessing_Boundary=Unclear. Non-stationarity and abrupt regime
transitions are explicitly discussed. No formal inferential statistical
test or economic/trading backtest was recovered. Public data availability
is stated; code is available only upon request.
